Hi Alex 
— great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

Call recap (30m):
- Primary goal: reduce inference cost/latency for FinWave chat assistants while keeping compliance and answer quality at enterprise levels.
- Current constraints: 99th %-ile latency target ~350ms for 2k context; throughput requirement ~200 concurrent requests; strict PII extraction accuracy requirements.
- Data: you shared the 1,000-user prompt set and a few hard-regex failure cases (thanks).

Recommended model & eval plan (high level):
1) Models to benchmark: Mistral-Theta-32B (base), Llama-3-70B (good baseline), and a tuned Mistral-17B variant for chat.
2) Quantization trade study: AWQ (8-bit+optimizations) as a high-throughput option; GPTQ (int4/int3) for quality-preserving compression; FP8 experimental for peak throughput but watch numeric stability on long chains.
3) Baselines to capture: unquantized top-performing run, AWQ-config (low-latency), GPTQ-config (quality-first).
4) Metrics: exact-match/EM on extraction tasks, BLEU/ROUGE for templates, and human-eval spot checks on 50 failure cases. Also measure p50/p95/p99 latency and server-side memory.

Suggested next steps / timeline:
- Today: we'll share the tradeoff doc + quick benchmark CSV. (Attachments included)
- This week: Redwood SE runs 1k prompt eval across the three model+quant configs and posts results.
- Next Tue: 30m call to review results and decide on a pilot config.

Action items:
- Alex: confirm access to the 1k prompt set and that we can run it under your test account (or provide a test snapshot).
- Marissa (me): schedule next review & share tradeoff doc + links.
- Monica & Nikhil: run initial trade study and surface any quality regressions on extraction tasks.

Attachments: quantization_tradeoffs_awq_vs_gptq.pdf, eval_results_finwave_1k_prompts_20280310.csv, recommended_prompt_set_finwave.txt

Alex — great, thanks. Quick technical notes and the numbers you asked for. See inline below.

On Mar 15, 2028, at 10:12 AM, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (call recap and attachments)

Summary: we ran the initial 1k prompt eval across three model configurations this morning. Results are attached (eval_results_finwave_1k_prompts_20280310.csv) and a high-level tradeoffs PDF is in the attachments/Drive link. Highlights: 

- Throughput / latency (approx vs unquantized baseline):
  - AWQ (8-bit optimized): p50 ~ -30% latency, p95 ~ -25%, throughput +45% — quality loss generally small on template extraction tasks (~1-2% EM drop), observed on long-chain reasoning examples.
  - GPTQ (aggressive int4): p50 ~ -45% latency, p95 ~ -40%, throughput +70% — quality impact higher on some prompt patterns; EM drop up to 4-6% on edge cases.
  - FP8 (experimental HW float8): p50 ~ -55% latency, p95 ~ -50%, throughput +90% — best for raw throughput but observed instability on numerically-sensitive prompts; recommend A/B testing only.

- Quality notes:
  - Extraction tasks: GPTQ kept format fidelity for short templates but began dropping tokenization-sensitive fields under complex prompts. AWQ tends to preserve token-level fidelity better.
  - Long-context reasoning: both AWQ and GPTQ show degradation as chain length increases; recommend caching prefix outputs and using a larger context model where accuracy matters.

- Recommended pilot configuration for FinWave:
  1) Baseline: Mistral-Theta-32B unquantized for 10% of traffic (quality canaries).
  2) Primary: Mistral-17B + AWQ for 70% traffic (good throughput with minimal quality loss).
  3) Burst/Batch: GPTQ Llama-3-70B for heavy throughput batch jobs where slight drop is acceptable.

- Compliance one-pager: short doc attached in Drive link and we can emit the example audit logs you requested via our Private deployment logging hook.

Actionables we executed:
- Uploaded CSV of 1k eval results to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/quantization-tradeoffs-20280310
- Added a recommended prompt-set file: recommended_prompt_set_finwave.txt
- Created an Eval run in Redwood: https://app.redwood.ai/run/benchmark/finwave-1k (results & plots).

Next steps we propose:
- Monica/Nikhil: pair with your infra engineer to validate memory footprints and provide an infra sizing spreadsheet (we’ll send by EOD tomorrow).
- FinWave: review the attached CSV/plots and flag any 50 edge cases you want to prioritize for manual review.
- Marissa: schedule the Tuesday follow-up (send calendar invite when FinWave confirms a slot).

Let me know if you want a quick 15m walkthrough of the CSV and plots — happy to jump on a call.
